# The Manual

> Boldly Read What No Dev Has Read Before

Comprehensive Documentation for Engineers Aiming for the Stars 💫

Guides for legacy setups and API reference for `@warp-drive/legacy`, `@ember-data/adapter`, `@ember-data/active-record`, `@ember-data/debug`, `@ember-data/legacy-compat`, `@ember-data/model`, `@ember-data/json-api`, `@ember-data/store`, `@ember-data/graph`, `@ember-data/request`, `@ember-data/request-utils`, `@ember-data/rest`, `@ember-data/serializer`, `@ember-data/tracking`, `@warp-drive/core-types`, `@warp-drive/build-config`, `@warp-drive/schema-record` are indexed separately in https://canary.warp-drive.io/llms-legacy.txt, with full text in https://canary.warp-drive.io/llms-legacy-full.txt.

## Table of Contents

### Installation

- [Instructions](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/installation.md): Install @warp-drive/core and @warp-drive/json-api with exact pinned versions, then add the reactivity package and install import for Ember, React, or TC39 Signals.
- [UNPKG](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/installation/unpkg.md): Load prebuilt ESM builds of WarpDrive packages from UNPKG and pick the unpkg, unpkg-dev, unpkg-deprecated, or unpkg-dev-deprecated export condition you need.

### Configuration

- [Setup](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/configuration.md): Set up WarpDrive's babel build plugin with compatWith and create a store with useRecommendedStore or useLegacyStore, the two steps required before making any request.
- [Setup - Advanced](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/configuration/advanced.md): Build a Store class by hand, adding RequestManager, SchemaService, JSONAPICache, instantiateRecord, and DefaultCachePolicy step by step, with Ember Model and migration variants.
- [Setup - React](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/configuration/react.md): Provide your WarpDrive store to React components with StoreProvider, read it with useStore, and know when a component re-renders.

### Tutorials

- [Overview](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/tutorials.md): Learn WarpDrive by building apps step by step, starting with the data layer of a TodoMVC app in Ember, written one request at a time.

#### TodoMVC

- [0. Setup](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/tutorials/todomvc.md): Build the data layer of a TodoMVC app with WarpDrive and Ember. Create the starter with npx @warp-drive/tutorials, run it, and see where you'll write WarpDrive code.
- [1. First request](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/tutorials/todomvc/first-request.md): Request the todos with store.request, then render the Future it returns with a <Request> block.
- [2. Why that worked](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/tutorials/todomvc/why-that-worked.md): The four ideas WarpDrive is built on: requests instead of models, one path for every request, one cached copy of each thing, and read-only records.
- [3. Request builders](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/tutorials/todomvc/request-builders.md): Write each request once, as a builder, and give every request the JSON:API headers with a handler.
- [4. Create](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/tutorials/todomvc/create.md): Create a todo with one request, and let cache invalidation refetch every todo list for you.
- [5. Edit title](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/tutorials/todomvc/edit-title.md): See how each todo becomes an editable copy, then save a new title with one request that every list shows.
- [6. Toggle](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/tutorials/todomvc/toggle.md): Save a todo's completed state, then move it between the Active and Completed lists yourself by patching the cache.
- [7. Delete](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/tutorials/todomvc/delete.md): Delete a todo with one request, and let the cache drop it from every list.
- [8. Bulk operations](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/tutorials/todomvc/bulk-operations.md): Toggle or clear many todos with one request each, and update the cache yourself when the response doesn't say what changed.

### The Manual

- [Introduction](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides.md): Learn what WarpDrive offers as a framework-agnostic data layer, from fine-grained reactivity and Fetch-style requests to schemas, the relational cache, mutations, and handlers.
- [Community Resources](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/the-manual/community-resources.md): Find conference talks, blog posts, and podcasts about WarpDrive and EmberData from 2019 onward, and learn how to add your own to the list via PR.

#### Requests

- [Making Requests](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/requests.md): Start here to make requests with store.request, the <Request /> component, and getRequestState, then set RequestInfo options and chain handlers in a RequestManager.
- [Typing Requests](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/requests/typing-requests.md): Type request responses in builders with withResponseType and withReactiveResponse, without casting, including the ReactiveDataDocument meta, errors, and error-meta type params.
- [Using The Response](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/requests/using-the-response.md): Read the Future a request returns, use its lid, getStream, and abort, handle FetchError rejections, and know when content is a ReactiveDocument.
- [Builders](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/requests/builders.md): Write documented, well-named builder functions that form a typed, cross-framework SDK for your API, produce stable RequestKeys, and drive the Request component and your own components.
- [Handlers](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/requests/handlers.md): Write a Handler middleware that calls next and normalizes a REST response into a JSON:API document with dasherize and singularize so the cache can consume it.

#### Schemas

- [Overview](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/schemas.md): Start here for the schemas section to see how a ResourceSchema maps raw cached fields to camelCase reactive properties and relationships, then pick LegacyMode or PolarisMode.
- [ObjectSchemas](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/schemas/object-schemas.md): Define an embedded ObjectSchema with a null identity, reference it from a resource via a `schema-object` field, and register it with `registerResource` so nested data is reactive.
- [SimpleFields](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/schemas/simple-fields.md): Declare primitive string, number, boolean, or date attributes on a ResourceSchema or ObjectSchema as `field` kinds and attach a `type` to route them through a Transformation.
- [Relational Fields](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/schemas/relational-fields.md): Placeholder for the guide to relational fields such as `resource`, `collection`, `belongsTo`, and `hasMany` on a ResourceSchema; no content yet.
- [Complex Fields](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/schemas/complex-fields.md): Embed nested objects and lists inside a resource with `schema-object` and `schema-array` fields backed by an identity-less ObjectSchema, keeping every nested value reactive.
- [Traits](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/schemas/traits.md): Group reusable fields such as timestamps into a Trait, register it with `registerTrait`, and merge it into any ResourceSchema by listing its name in the `traits` array.
- [Derivations](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/schemas/derivations.md): Define memoized read-only `derived` fields, register the derivation function by its `Type` key on the store, and spot when relational or optional data makes it the wrong tool.
- [Transformations](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/schemas/transformations.md): Convert one field between its cache shape and app shape by writing a Transformation with `hydrate`, `serialize`, and `defaultValue`, then register it via `useRecommendedStore`.
- [Extensions](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/schemas/extensions.md): Placeholder for the guide to schema extensions, which add custom methods and properties to reactive arrays, objects, and resources during migration; no content yet.

##### Resources

- [ResourceSchemas](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/schemas/resources.md): Create a top-level ResourceSchema with `withDefaults`, choose `field`, `resource`, `collection`, or `schema-object` kinds, register it, and pick LegacyMode or PolarisMode.
- [LegacyMode (recommended)](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/schemas/resources/legacy-mode.md): Emulate Model with ReactiveResource in LegacyMode using `attribute`, `belongsTo`, and `hasMany` fields, `registerDerivations` from `@warp-drive/legacy`, and `WithLegacy` types.
- [PolarisMode (preview)](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/schemas/resources/polaris-mode.md): Decide whether to try preview PolarisMode by weighing its immutable records and explicit editing against its current relationship and state-property limitations.

#### Relational Data

- [Overview](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/relational-data.md): Start here to configure relationships in WarpDrive; links each cardinality page from one-to-none through many-to-many plus the inverses, LinksMode, and polymorphism guides.

##### Configuration

- [Many To Many Relationships](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/relational-data/configuration/many-to-many.md): Define a bidirectional many-to-many hasMany relationship with a managed inverse, or split it into two many-to-none collections, via Model, JSON schema, or LegacyMode withDefaults.
- [Many To None Relationships](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/relational-data/configuration/many-to-none.md): Define a unidirectional many-to-none hasMany relationship with inverse null, for collections whose other side is too large to track, via Model, JSON schema, or LegacyMode.
- [Many To One Relationships](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/relational-data/configuration/many-to-one.md): Configure a many-to-one relationship, which WarpDrive treats as the one-to-many configuration viewed from the belongsTo side; this stub redirects to that page.
- [One To Many Relationships](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/relational-data/configuration/one-to-many.md): Define a bidirectional one-to-many relationship pairing belongsTo with hasMany and managed inverses, or split it into one-to-none plus many-to-none, via Model or schema.
- [One To None Relationships](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/relational-data/configuration/one-to-none.md): Define a unidirectional one-to-none belongsTo relationship with inverse null and learn how WarpDrive tracks its implicit inverse, via Model, JSON schema, or LegacyMode.
- [One To One Relationships](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/relational-data/configuration/one-to-one.md): Define a bidirectional one-to-one relationship with belongsTo on both sides and managed inverses, or split it into two one-to-none relationships, via Model or schema.

##### Features

- [Relationship Inverses](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/relational-data/features/inverses.md): Placeholder for the guide to relationship inverses, how WarpDrive keeps both sides of a relationship in sync; still under construction, with no content yet.
- [Relationship Polymorphism](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/relational-data/features/polymorphism.md): Define open or closed polymorphic relationships using the polymorphic, inverse, and as field options on Model or schema, and handle abstract-to-concrete type upgrades on fetch.

#### Caching

- [Overview](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/caching.md): Understand how the CacheHandler resolves a RequestKey, applies CachePolicy for staleness, and stores responses, resources, fields, and relationships by replace or upsert.
- [Key Terminology](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/caching/key-terms.md): Learn the difference between StructuredDocument, ResourceDocument, and ReactiveDocument, and what ResourceType, ResourceKey, ResourceSchema, and Collection mean.

#### Reactivity

- [Overview](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/reactivity.md): Understand how WarpDrive uses signals as side-signals or gates to notify consumers of cache changes while letting you plug in your own or your framework's signals implementation.
- [Async as Reactive State](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/reactivity/derivation.md): Replace tracked loading, error, and value properties with getPromiseState and the Await component so a component stores a promise and derives pending, error, and success state.
- [Reactive Control Flow](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/reactivity/control-flow.md): Render request states declaratively with the Request component or getRequestState in Ember and React, handling loading, error, and retry without imperative async/await.

#### TypeScript

- [Overview](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/typescript.md): Start here to opt in to WarpDrive's alpha-stage TypeScript types, then follow the installation, configuration, brands, model typing, and includes typing pages in order.
- [Typing Includes](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/typescript/typing-includes.md): Type relationship-path include strings with the `Includes` and `StringSatisfiesIncludes` utils and `createIncludeValidator` so typos in includes fail at compile time.
- [WarpDrive's Types Strategy](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/typescript/why-brands.md): Understand why WarpDrive brands classes with a `Type` symbol and passes them as generics to `findRecord` instead of using type registries or class tokens.

#### Debugging

- [Overview](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/debugging.md): Enable WarpDrive's regionalized debug logging with `setWarpDriveLogging` at runtime or via build config, using flags such as LOG_REQUESTS, LOG_CACHE, and LOG_GRAPH.

#### Testing with Holodeck

- [Overview](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/testing.md)
- [Server Setup](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/testing/server-setup.md)
- [Client Setup](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/testing/client-setup.md)
- [Test Framework Integration](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/testing/test-framework-integration.md)
- [Writing Mocks](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/testing/writing-mocks.md)
- [Recording and Replaying](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/testing/record-and-replay.md)
- [Troubleshooting](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/testing/troubleshooting.md)
- [HoloPrograms](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/testing/holo-programs.md)

##### Common Setups

- [Common Setups](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/testing/common-setups.md): Serve the test page and the holodeck mock server from one origin, so mocked requests need no CORS and no preflight, with the forwarder that Vite, testem, and Caddy setups share.
- [Vite Dev Server](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/testing/common-setups/vite.md): Forward holodeck's requests through the Vite dev server with a five-line plugin, so the suite you open at /tests runs on one origin.
- [Testem](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/testing/common-setups/testem.md): Forward holodeck's requests through testem's own server with its middleware option, so the suite pnpm test runs has one origin.
- [Caddy](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/testing/common-setups/caddy.md): Put Caddy in front of the Vite dev server and holodeck, so the test page is served over HTTPS on one origin with the certificate holodeck already has.

#### Mutations

- [Overview](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/mutations.md): Start here for how-to patterns on changing data in WarpDrive; routes to the Mutating State and Patching The Cache pages, both of which are still under construction.
- [Mutations](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/mutations/mutations.md): Placeholder for the Mutating State how-to on changing records and relationships through the Store; still under construction, with no content yet.
- [Operations](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/mutations/operations.md): Placeholder for the Patching The Cache how-to on applying operations directly to the cache; still under construction, with no content yet.

#### Experiments

- [Experiments](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/experiments.md): Browse WarpDrive's experimental, pre-RFC features that may change or be removed, currently Storage Resources and Pagination, and pick which one to read next.
- [Pagination](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/experiments/pagination.md): Paginate a collection with the experimental `getPaginationState` primitives and the `<Paginate />` and `<EachLink />` Ember components in paged or infinite mode.
- [Storage Resources](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/experiments/storage-resources.md): Persist reactive class fields to localStorage or sessionStorage with the experimental `LocalResource`, `SessionResource`, `field`, `effect`, and `param` decorators.

#### Cookbook

- [Overview](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/cookbook.md): Start here for short, self-contained WarpDrive recipes, such as basic request usage, auth handlers, and choosing singular or plural resource types, and find where the upgrade guides live.
- [Auth Handler](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/cookbook/auth-handlers.md): Write a request `Handler` that adds JWT bearer tokens or CSRF tokens to outgoing requests, including an Ember class-based handler with injected services.
- [Requests](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/cookbook/basic-usage.md): Build a `RequestManager` with the `Fetch` handler, configure `setBuildURLConfig`, issue a JSON:API `query` request, page through results, and handle errors.
- [Holodeck in Dev Mode](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/cookbook/holodeck-in-dev-mode.md)
- [Using Ember and React on the Same Page](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/cookbook/multiple-frameworks-on-one-page.md): Import @warp-drive/alien-signals/install before the Ember and React install entry points so one WarpDrive store re-renders both Ember and React components on the same page.
- [Resource Type Naming: singular or plural? What to choose? Why is that?](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/cookbook/naming-conventions.md): Decide whether resource types should be singular or plural and dasherized or snake_case, and keep that one `type` string the same across API responses, ResourceSchemas, relationship fields and request builders.
- [Paginating POST Queries](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/the-manual/cookbook/paginating-post-queries.md): Write a request handler that generates `next` links for a query sent as a `POST` or `QUERY`, so `next()` and the pagination primitives work when the server can't return links itself.

### FAQ

- [Index](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/faq.md): Find short answers to common questions about adopting and configuring WarpDrive, each linking to the guide that covers the topic in depth.
- [Multiple Frameworks on One Page](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/faq/multiple-frameworks.md): Learn how to use more than one framework on the same page with WarpDrive by importing @warp-drive/alien-signals/install before each framework's install entry point.
- [PolarisMode With Ember and React](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/faq/polaris-mode-with-ember-and-react.md): Learn why an app rendering Ember and React on the same page can share a WarpDrive store in LegacyMode, and which Model fields won't re-render React components.

### Linting

- [Linting](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/linting.md): Install eslint-plugin-warp-drive and enable its recommended, template, and React flat configs, including the ember-eslint-parser setup that Glimmer template rules need.

### Contributing

- [Become A Contributor](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/contributing/become-a-contributor.md): Start contributing to WarpDrive itself: find the issue tracker, RFC label, and Discord, then follow links to project setup, architecture, docs, and the RFC process.
- [Reporting Issues](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/contributing/issues.md): Report a WarpDrive bug through GitHub issues using the repo's issue template, and know to ask on Discord first when unsure whether something is a bug.
- [Setting Up The Project](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/contributing/setting-up-the-project.md): Set up a WarpDrive contributor checkout: install mise, pnpm, and mkcert, run `pnpm install`, create holodeck certs, and use `pnpm start` plus `pnpm sync` while developing.
- [Project Architecture](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/contributing/project-architecture.md): See how WarpDrive's packages and primitives fit together through interface-driven boundaries, via an architectural diagram for contributors to the library itself.
- [Key Concepts](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/contributing/key-concepts.md): Choose the right identity type in WarpDrive internals: ResourceIdentifier, RecordIdentifier, or ResourceKey, based on whether lid is required and must be stable.
- [Submitting PRs](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/contributing/submitting-prs.md): Open a PR against WarpDrive main with the right tests, a title like `feat: ...` that auto-applies its `:label:` changelog label, and `target:` labels for any backports.
- [The RFC Process](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/contributing/rfc-process.md): Propose a WarpDrive feature or deprecation: discuss it on Discord, draft from rfcs/0000-template.md, open a PR labeled `:label: rfc`, and shepherd it through emberjs/rfcs.
- [Performing A Release](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/contributing/RELEASE.md): Perform a WarpDrive release from the GitHub Actions workflow: order the lts, release, beta, and canary channels, then polish the GitHub release notes and announce it.
- [The Project Roadmap](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/guides/contributing/ROADMAP.md): Check which Polaris edition goals WarpDrive has shipped or still has open, what is planned beyond Polaris, and which features and deprecations land in each 5.x release.

#### Writing Documentation

- [Overview](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/contributing/writing-documentation.md): Which type of doc to write for a change, who each type is for, how the docs site is built from the repo, and the checks to run before opening the PR.
- [Writing Guides](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/contributing/writing-documentation/writing-guides.md): How to write a tutorial, concept, or reference guide for the docs site, where the files live, and what frontmatter and tags shape the Markdown that coding agents read.
- [Writing API Docs](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/contributing/writing-documentation/writing-api-docs.md): How to write the TSDoc comments that become the API reference, including which tags to use, the @summary each API page needs, usage examples, and what stays out of the published docs.
- [Writing Agent Skills](https://canary.warp-drive.io/guides/contributing/writing-documentation/writing-agent-skills.md): How to add or change a skill in @warp-drive/memory-alpha so coding agents find and follow it, including the routing tables, file rules, and checks.

### RFCs

- [Transactional Notification Delivery and Reactive Request State](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/rfcs/0001-warp-drive-transactional-notifications.md): Proposes delivering all WarpDrive cache notifications in one synchronous batch at transaction close and rebuilding request state as signals-backed data.
- [A Framework-Agnostic Build Plugin for WarpDrive](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/rfcs/0002-warp-drive-build-plugin.md): Proposes a framework-agnostic `@warp-drive/core/build-plugin` bundler plugin that replaces the babel and @embroider/macros build configuration for WarpDrive.
- [A Browser Devtools Extension](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/rfcs/0003-warp-drive-devtools-extension.md): Proposes a Chrome and Firefox devtools extension for inspecting WarpDrive requests, cache, and schemas, attached via a production-strippable hook in @warp-drive/core.
- [Dropping V1 Addon and Classic ember-cli Macros Support in 6.0](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/rfcs/0004-drop-v1-addon-and-classic-macros-support.md)
- [Deprecating the Legacy ember-data Packages and @warp-drive/core-types](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/rfcs/0005-deprecate-legacy-packages.md): Proposes deprecating the ember-data package, every @ember-data/* package, and @warp-drive/core-types now, in favor of their already-shipping @warp-drive/* successors, with removal from publishing targeted for 6.0.
- [Pointer and Reference Fields](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/rfcs/0006-pointer-and-reference-fields.md): Proposes four PolarisMode relationship field kinds (pointer, pointer-array, reference, reference-array) for relationships WarpDrive never fetches or validates for delivery, where pointers assert the related resource is loaded and references tolerate its absence.
- [Virtualized Resources](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/rfcs/0007-virtualized-resources.md): Proposes virtual resource schemas, the frontend equivalent of a materialized view, whose fields reflect fields of other cached resources through pointers so that data read or written through the view stays consistent everywhere.
- [A $state Field for PolarisMode ReactiveResources](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/rfcs/0008-reactive-resource-state.md): Proposes adding a reactive, read-only $state field to the PolarisMode defaults that reports a resource's lifecycle state (new, empty, deleted, dirty) and its per-field local changes, replacing the LegacyMode state flags that still apply and dropping the ones that don't.
- [Deprecating Subscription-Based Request State](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/rfcs/0009-deprecate-request-state-subscriptions.md): Proposes deprecating the imperative RequestStateService subscription API in favor of the signals-backed reactive request state introduced by RFC 0001, with removal targeted for 6.0.

### Upgrading

#### ember-data → WarpDrive

- [Migrating from ember-data](https://canary.warp-drive.io/upgrading/ember-data.md): Move an app on ember-data 1.x through 4.12 to the latest WarpDrive one route at a time, running a second `@warp-drive/*` store beside ember-data until ember-data can be removed.
- [Replacing ember-data in place](https://canary.warp-drive.io/upgrading/ember-data/in-place.md): Replace ember-data 4.12 with the latest @warp-drive/* packages in one change, keeping the single store and the existing Models, adapters and serializers running, then convert to schemas and request builders at your own pace.

### Blog

#### 5.x

- [5.x](https://canary.warp-drive.io/blog/v5.md): Browse the WarpDrive blog posts published while 5.x was the current major version, newest first.
- [Introducing Upgrading & Blog](https://canary.warp-drive.io/blog/v5/introducing-upgrading-and-blog.md): Learn why WarpDrive 5.10 added the permanent Upgrading and Blog sections to warp-drive.io and where the former /guides/migrating/ pages now live.
- [WarpDrive 5.9](https://canary.warp-drive.io/blog/v5/warp-drive-5-9.md): Learn what changed in WarpDrive 5.9 — reactive pagination, the migrate-to-schema codemod, Memory Alpha for AI agents, and rolled-up types — and why to install 5.9.1 rather than 5.9.0.

### API Docs

- [@warp-drive/core](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/api/@warp-drive/core.md): The core WarpDrive package, providing the `Store`, the `RequestManager` and its handlers, the Cache interface, reactive resources and `useRecommendedStore` for app setup.
- [@warp-drive/json-api](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/api/@warp-drive/json-api.md): The recommended in-memory JSON:API document and resource cache for WarpDrive, `JSONAPICache`, which most apps pass to `useRecommendedStore`.
- [@warp-drive/utilities](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/api/@warp-drive/utilities.md): Request-building utilities for WarpDrive, including URL and query-param helpers such as `buildBaseURL` and ready-made request builders for JSON:API, REST and ActiveRecord APIs.
- [@warp-drive/experiments](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/api/@warp-drive/experiments.md): Experimental WarpDrive features not yet through an RFC, one entry point each, including the SharedWorker-based `DataWorker` and `ImageWorker`, browser storage and reactive pagination.
- [@warp-drive/ember](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/api/@warp-drive/ember.md): Ember bindings for WarpDrive, providing the `<Request />` and `<Await />` components for rendering request and promise states, Ember reactivity setup and experimental pagination.
- [@warp-drive/react](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/api/@warp-drive/react.md): React bindings for WarpDrive, providing `StoreProvider`, `useStore` and the `<Request />` component for rendering request states with React reactivity.
- [@warp-drive/tc39-proposal-signals](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/api/@warp-drive/tc39-proposal-signals.md): Configures WarpDrive reactivity to use the TC39 Signals polyfill (signal-polyfill); import its install entry in apps that use TC39 Signals.
- [@warp-drive/alien-signals](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/api/@warp-drive/alien-signals.md): Configures WarpDrive reactivity to use a signals graph built on alien-signals; import its install entry in apps, or build a framework integration on its primitives.
- [@warp-drive/holodeck](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/api/@warp-drive/holodeck.md): ⚡️ Simple, Fast HTTP Mocking for Tests: experimental mocking that makes real network requests and replays git-managed recordings, via `MockServerHandler` and the `GET`/`POST` helpers in `@warp-drive/holodeck/mock`.
- [@warp-drive/schema-dsl](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/api/@warp-drive/schema-dsl.md): TypeScript decorators such as `@Resource` and `@field` for authoring WarpDrive schemas as classes, compiled to plain JSON schemas at build time by a Vite plugin.
- [eslint-plugin-warp-drive](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/api/eslint-plugin-warp-drive.md): ESLint rules and a recommended flat config for apps using WarpDrive, catching invalid resource types, ids and relationships, legacy imports and discouraged request patterns.
- [@warp-drive/memory-alpha](https://canary.warp-drive.io/pr-preview/pr-11291/api/@warp-drive/memory-alpha.md): WarpDrive knowledge packaged as plain markdown skill files for AI coding agents, with no code or exports, to read directly or adapt into Claude Skills, MCP servers or editor rules.

#### @warp-drive/core

- [@warp-drive/core/build-config](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config.md): Build-time configuration for WarpDrive: `setConfig` and its babel plugin for deprecations, features, debug logging, and polyfill settings.
- [@warp-drive/core/configure](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/configure.md): Provides `setupSignals`, which tells WarpDrive which signal and reactivity library to build its reactive values on.
- [@warp-drive/core/reactive](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/reactive.md): Schema-driven reactive records, arrays, and documents the store builds from cached data, plus the `SchemaService` and schema types that define them.
- [@warp-drive/core/request](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/request.md): Request-layer types such as `Future`, `Handler` and `Context`, plus `withResponseType` and `withReactiveResponse` for typing the response a request resolves with.
- [@warp-drive/core/store](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/store.md): The `DefaultCachePolicy` and `parseCacheControl` for expiring cached requests, plus the `NotificationManager` type for subscribing to cache change notifications.
- [@warp-drive/core/types](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types.md): Shared WarpDrive types such as `ResourceKey`, `SchemaService`, `CacheCapabilitiesManager`, and the legacy finder option types.

##### exports

- [ConfiguredStore](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/classes/ConfiguredStore.md): Central coordinator that connects requests for data with schemas, the cache and reactivity.
- [RequestManager](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/classes/RequestManager.md): Runs each request through a chain of handlers that can fulfill, modify, or pass it along, and returns a `Future` for the response.
- [Store](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/classes/Store.md): Central coordinator that connects requests for data with schemas, the cache and reactivity.
- [CacheHandler](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/variables/CacheHandler.md): The RequestManager cache handler that serves, dedupes, and caches store requests and returns reactive documents when hydration is enabled.
- [Fetch](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/variables/Fetch.md): Terminal request handler that sends the request with native `fetch` and resolves with the parsed JSON body, turning HTTP failures into errors.
- [recordIdentifierFor()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/functions/recordIdentifierFor.md): Returns the stable `ResourceKey` (type, id, and lid) the store assigned to a record instance.
- [setIdentifierForgetMethod()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/functions/setIdentifierForgetMethod.md): Registers a callback run when the store releases a resource key, for cleaning up your own lookup tables.
- [setIdentifierGenerationMethod()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/functions/setIdentifierGenerationMethod.md): Overrides how the store generates `lid` cache keys for resources and documents; must be set before the store is created.
- [setIdentifierResetMethod()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/functions/setIdentifierResetMethod.md): Registers a callback run when the store's key cache is torn down, for resetting any custom key-generation state.
- [setIdentifierUpdateMethod()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/functions/setIdentifierUpdateMethod.md): Registers a callback run when an existing resource key receives new data, for updating your own secondary lookup tables.
- [setKeyInfoForResource()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/functions/setKeyInfoForResource.md): Overrides how the store derives the `type` and `id` of a new `ResourceKey` from resource data; must be set before the store is created.
- [useRecommendedStore()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/functions/useRecommendedStore.md): Builds a Store subclass preconfigured with the given cache, schemas, and handlers, plus `Fetch`, `CacheHandler`, and a default cache policy.

##### /build-config

- [@warp-drive/core/build-config/babel-macros](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/babel-macros.md): The `macros` function, which returns the Babel plugins that strip WarpDrive deprecation, canary-feature, debug-logging and env code at build time.
- [@warp-drive/core/build-config/canary-features](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/canary-features.md): Build-time flags, such as `JSON_API_CACHE_VALIDATION_ERRORS`, that gate unreleased WarpDrive features for canary builds.
- [@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging.md): Debug-only logging flags, such as `LOG_CACHE` and `LOG_REQUESTS`, set in build config or at runtime via `setWarpDriveLogging`.
- [@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations.md): Deprecation flags, such as `DEPRECATE_NON_STRICT_TYPES`, that keep deprecated WarpDrive behavior active until the build config drops it by `compatWith` version or by flag.

###### exports

- [babelPlugin()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/functions/babelPlugin.md): Creates the Babel plugins that apply a WarpDrive build config, for projects not already using `@embroider/macros`.
- [setConfig()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/functions/setConfig.md): Applies a WarpDrive build config through `@embroider/macros`, controlling env behavior, logging, deprecated-code stripping, and canary features.

###### /babel-macros

####### exports

- [macros()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/babel-macros/functions/macros.md): Returns the Babel plugin entries that turn WarpDrive deprecation, canary-feature, debug-logging, env, and assert imports into build-time code-stripping macros.

###### /canary-features

####### exports

- [ENFORCE_STRICT_RESOURCE_FINALIZATION](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/canary-features/variables/ENFORCE_STRICT_RESOURCE_FINALIZATION.md): Canary feature flag that throws in development when `schema.fields` is first called for a resource whose traits, or its traits' traits, are missing.
- [JSON_API_CACHE_VALIDATION_ERRORS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/canary-features/variables/JSON_API_CACHE_VALIDATION_ERRORS.md): Canary feature flag that makes the JSON:API cache validate payloads given to `cache.put` against registered schemas and the JSON:API spec.

###### /debugging

####### exports

- [DEBUG_RELATIONSHIP_NOTIFICATIONS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/DEBUG_RELATIONSHIP_NOTIFICATIONS.md): Debug logging flag that logs why a change notification fired while processing an update to a hasMany relationship.
- [LOG_CACHE](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/LOG_CACHE.md): Debug logging flag that logs cache updates to both local and remote state; it replaces `LOG_PAYLOADS`, `LOG_OPERATIONS`, and `LOG_MUTATIONS`.
- [LOG_CACHE_POLICY](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/LOG_CACHE_POLICY.md): Debug logging flag that logs the decisions the default CachePolicy makes about whether cached requests are expired or stale.
- [LOG_GRAPH](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/LOG_GRAPH.md): Debug logging flag that logs the updates the relationship graph receives.
- [LOG_IDENTIFIERS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/LOG_IDENTIFIERS.md): Debug logging flag that logs lookups, generation, and updates of the identifiers (cache keys) WarpDrive assigns to resources.
- [LOG_INSTANCE_CACHE](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/LOG_INSTANCE_CACHE.md): Debug logging flag that logs when the store creates or removes record instances and their cache entries.
- [LOG_METRIC_COUNTS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/LOG_METRIC_COUNTS.md): Debug logging flag that logs counts of key internal operations, for performance debugging.
- [LOG_MUTATIONS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/LOG_MUTATIONS.md): Removed debug logging flag that no longer has any effect; use `LOG_CACHE` to log cache updates instead.
- [LOG_NOTIFICATIONS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/LOG_NOTIFICATIONS.md): Debug logging flag that logs the change notifications the store's NotificationManager receives and delivers to subscribers.
- [LOG_OPERATIONS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/LOG_OPERATIONS.md): Removed debug logging flag that no longer has any effect; use `LOG_CACHE` to log cache updates instead.
- [LOG_PAYLOADS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/LOG_PAYLOADS.md): Removed debug logging flag that no longer has any effect; use `LOG_CACHE` to log cache updates instead.
- [LOG_REACT_SIGNAL_INTEGRATION](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/LOG_REACT_SIGNAL_INTEGRATION.md): Debug logging flag that logs how the React integration watches signals and notifies React of updates, for debugging React reactivity issues.
- [LOG_REQUEST_STATUS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/LOG_REQUEST_STATUS.md): Debug logging flag meant to log status updates for requests the store sends to the network (adapter); it currently has no effect.
- [LOG_REQUESTS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/variables/LOG_REQUESTS.md): Debug logging flag that logs each request issued through the RequestManager.

####### /Namespaces

- [@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/t](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/debugging/namespaces/t.md)

###### /deprecations

####### exports

- [DEPRECATE_COMPUTED_CHAINS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations/variables/DEPRECATE_COMPUTED_CHAINS.md): Planned deprecation flag, with no deprecation ID yet, guarding support for observer and computed chains on WarpDrive record arrays and ManyArrays.
- [DEPRECATE_EMBER_INFLECTOR](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations/variables/DEPRECATE_EMBER_INFLECTOR.md): Deprecation flag for using ember-inflector for pluralization and singularization instead of the `@ember-data/request-utils/string` utilities.
- [DEPRECATE_LEGACY_IMPORTS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations/variables/DEPRECATE_LEGACY_IMPORTS.md): Deprecation flag for importing from the legacy `ember-data/*` paths instead of `@ember-data/*`, except `ember-data/store`.
- [DEPRECATE_MANY_ARRAY_DUPLICATES](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations/variables/DEPRECATE_MANY_ARRAY_DUPLICATES.md): Deprecation flag for adding duplicate records to a ManyArray; when `false`, adding duplicates throws an error instead of being deduped.
- [DEPRECATE_NON_STRICT_ID](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations/variables/DEPRECATE_NON_STRICT_ID.md): Deprecation flag for legacy support of numeric resource IDs that are coerced to strings; set it to `false` once resolved to strip that support.
- [DEPRECATE_NON_STRICT_TYPES](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations/variables/DEPRECATE_NON_STRICT_TYPES.md): Deprecation flag for resource `type` values that are not non-empty, singular, dasherized strings; set it to `false` once resolved to strip that support.
- [DEPRECATE_NON_UNIQUE_PAYLOADS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations/variables/DEPRECATE_NON_UNIQUE_PAYLOADS.md): Deprecation flag for hasMany relationship payloads containing duplicate identifiers, which were silently de-duped and will instead error.
- [DEPRECATE_RELATIONSHIP_REMOTE_UPDATE_CLEARING_LOCAL_STATE](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations/variables/DEPRECATE_RELATIONSHIP_REMOTE_UPDATE_CLEARING_LOCAL_STATE.md): Deprecation flag for remote relationship updates discarding unsaved local changes; set it to `false`, or `resetOnRemoteUpdate: false`, to keep them.
- [DEPRECATE_STORE_EXTENDS_EMBER_OBJECT](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations/variables/DEPRECATE_STORE_EXTENDS_EMBER_OBJECT.md): Deprecation flag controlling whether the Store extends `@ember/object`; set it to `false` to stop extending EmberObject.
- [DEPRECATE_TRACKING_PACKAGE](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations/variables/DEPRECATE_TRACKING_PACKAGE.md): Deprecation flag for the `@ember-data/tracking` package, which is replaced by the Ember reactivity setup in `@warp-drive/ember/install`.
- [DISABLE_7X_DEPRECATIONS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations/variables/DISABLE_7X_DEPRECATIONS.md): Opt-in flag: set it to `false` to make deprecations backported from 6.x print and become resolvable; by default they stay silent and unresolvable.
- [ENABLE_LEGACY_REQUEST_METHODS](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations/variables/ENABLE_LEGACY_REQUEST_METHODS.md): Deprecation flag for store request methods like `findRecord`, `query`, and `saveRecord` that bypass `store.request()`; `false` strips them.
- [ENABLE_LEGACY_SCHEMA_SERVICE](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/build-config/deprecations/variables/ENABLE_LEGACY_SCHEMA_SERVICE.md): Deprecation flag that keeps the legacy schema service APIs, such as `registerSchemaDefinitionService`, enabled while warning when they are used.

##### /configure

###### exports

- [registerSignals()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/configure/functions/registerSignals.md): Registers signal hooks with the configured composing implementation, or configures them with `setupSignals` when there is none.
- [setupSignals()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/configure/functions/setupSignals.md): Registers the signal hooks WarpDrive uses for reactivity, built by a callback that receives `HooksOptions`.

##### /reactive

###### exports

- [SchemaService](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/reactive/classes/SchemaService.md): The default schema service, which stores resource and object schemas, traits, derivations, transformations, hash functions and extensions registered at runtime.
- [Checkout](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/reactive/variables/Checkout.md): Deprecated symbol-keyed method on a ReactiveResource that resolves with an editable copy; use `checkout` instead.
- [fromIdentity](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/reactive/variables/fromIdentity.md): The `@identity` derivation, which reads a record's `id`, `lid`, `type`, or whole resource key for use in derived fields.
- [checkout()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/reactive/functions/checkout.md): Resolves with an editable copy of an immutable `ReactiveResource` so its fields can be changed locally.
- [commit()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/reactive/functions/commit.md): Forcibly makes an editable resource's local changes its new remote (immutable) state, bypassing a save round-trip.
- [createRequestSubscription()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/reactive/functions/createRequestSubscription.md): Creates a reactive subscription to a request or query that tracks its state and handles autorefresh, retry, and refresh.
- [getPromiseState()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/reactive/functions/getPromiseState.md): Returns a cached, reactive state object tracking whether a promise is pending, fulfilled, or rejected, for use in JS or templates.
- [getRequestState()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/reactive/functions/getRequestState.md): Returns a cached, reactive state object tracking a request `Future` through pending, success, error, and cancellation.
- [instantiateRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/reactive/functions/instantiateRecord.md): Default store `instantiateRecord` hook that creates a `ReactiveResource` for a resource key from its registered schema.
- [registerDerivations()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/reactive/functions/registerDerivations.md): Registers the `@identity` and `@constructor` derivations that schemas built with `withDefaults` depend on.
- [teardownRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/reactive/functions/teardownRecord.md): Default store `teardownRecord` hook that destroys a `ReactiveResource` when the store releases it.
- [withDefaults()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/reactive/functions/withDefaults.md): Adds the default `id` identity plus `$key`, `$type`, and `constructor` derived fields to a PolarisMode resource schema.

##### /request

###### exports

- [withBrand](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/request/variables/withBrand.md): Deprecated alias for `withResponseType`, which types a request object with its expected response type.
- [createDeferred()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/request/functions/createDeferred.md): Creates a promise together with its `resolve` and `reject` callbacks so it can be handed out before it is settled.
- [getPromiseResult()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/request/functions/getPromiseResult.md): Synchronously returns the settled value or error previously recorded for a promise, or `undefined` if none was recorded.
- [setPromiseResult()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/request/functions/setPromiseResult.md): Records a promise's settled value or error so it can later be read synchronously with `getPromiseResult`.
- [withReactiveResponse()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/request/functions/withReactiveResponse.md): Types a request object so its response resolves as a `ReactiveDataDocument` of the given data and meta types; no runtime effect.
- [withResponseType()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/request/functions/withResponseType.md): Types a request object with the response type that `store.request` or `RequestManager.request` should resolve with; no runtime effect.

##### /store

###### exports

- [DefaultCachePolicy](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/store/classes/DefaultCachePolicy.md): The built-in cache policy, which expires cached requests using expiration headers or time since the response `date`, and invalidates queries after matching creates.
- [parseCacheControl()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/store/functions/parseCacheControl.md): Parses a `Cache-Control` header string into a `CacheControlValue` object, caching results per header string.

##### /types

- [@warp-drive/core/types/cache](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/cache.md): The `Cache` interface a cache implementation fulfills to store, patch, mutate and read documents and resources, plus the `ChangedAttributesHash` and `RelationshipDiff` types.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/graph](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/graph.md): Types for the operations that update a relationship's remote (persisted) or local (uncommitted) state in the relationship Graph.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/identifier](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/identifier.md): Types for the stable keys that reference cached data, `ResourceKey` for resources and `RequestKey` for request documents, plus their deprecated identifier aliases.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/params](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/params.md): Types for the query params request builders serialize into a URL and the options that control how arrays are serialized.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/record](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/record.md): Types for records that declare their resource type via the `[Type]` symbol, including `TypedRecordInstance`, `Includes`, `Mask` and the `createIncludeValidator` helper.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/request](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/request.md): Types for requests and responses: `RequestInfo`, the request shapes builders return, cache options, the handler context and the documents a request's `Future` settles with.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/symbols](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/symbols.md): Symbol keys WarpDrive uses on records and requests, such as `Type` to brand a record with its resource type and `RequestSignature` to type a request's response.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/utils](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/utils.md): Generic TypeScript utility types: `WithPartial` to make named properties optional and `Mutable` to strip `readonly`.

###### /cache

- [@warp-drive/core/types/cache/aliases](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/cache/aliases.md): The `ResourceBlob` type for opaque raw resource data whose format the Cache defines.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/cache/change](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/cache/change.md): The `Change` type describing one upsert or removal of a resource or document recorded by the cache.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/cache/mutations](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/cache/mutations.md): Types for the mutations `cache.mutate` applies to a relationship's local (uncommitted) state, such as adding, removing, replacing or sorting related resources.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/cache/operations](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/cache/operations.md): Types for the operations passed to `cache.patch` to update the cache's remote (clean) state, such as from WebSocket or server-sent event messages.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/cache/relationship](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/cache/relationship.md): Types for the cache-side state of to-one and to-many relationships, with related resources referenced by `ResourceKey`.

###### /json

- [@warp-drive/core/types/json/raw](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/json/raw.md): Types for JSON values: `PrimitiveValue`, `ObjectValue`, `ArrayValue` and their `Value` union.

###### /record

####### exports

- [createIncludeValidator()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/record/functions/createIncludeValidator.md): Returns a function that type-checks a comma-separated `include` string against the valid relationship paths of a record type and returns it unchanged.

###### /request

####### exports

- [EnableHydration](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/request/variables/EnableHydration.md): Symbol flag on a request that makes the CacheHandler return reactive records instead of raw cache documents; `store.request` sets it automatically.
- [SkipCache](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/request/variables/SkipCache.md): Symbol key for a request's `cacheOptions` that, when true, makes the request bypass the CacheHandler so it neither resolves from nor updates the cache.

###### /schema

- [@warp-drive/core/types/schema/concepts](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/schema/concepts.md): Types for the functions schemas reference by name: `Transformation` to convert field values, `Derivation` for computed fields and `HashFn` for object identity.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/schema/fields](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/schema/fields.md): Types for every field schema kind and for PolarisMode and LegacyMode resource, object and trait schemas, plus the `resourceSchema` and `objectSchema` helpers and type guards.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/schema/schema-service](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/schema/schema-service.md): The `SchemaService` interface a store's schema service implements to describe resource types, traits, fields and derivations, plus the legacy `AttributesSchema` and `RelationshipsSchema` types.

####### /fields

######## exports

- [isLegacyResourceSchema()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/schema/fields/functions/isLegacyResourceSchema.md): Type guard that returns true when a schema is a LegacyMode resource schema, meaning it is a resource schema with `legacy: true`.
- [isResourceSchema()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/schema/fields/functions/isResourceSchema.md): Type guard that returns true when a schema is a resource schema, meaning its identity field is of kind `@id`.
- [objectSchema()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/schema/fields/functions/objectSchema.md): Returns the given object schema unchanged, typed so its definition is type-checked.
- [resourceSchema()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/schema/fields/functions/resourceSchema.md): Returns the given resource schema unchanged, typed so its definition is type-checked; relationship inverses and related types are not validated.

###### /spec

- [@warp-drive/core/types/spec/document](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/spec/document.md): Types for the raw {json:api} documents the cache stores and returns for a request: meta-only, single-resource, collection and error documents.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/spec/error](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/spec/error.md): The `ApiError` type for one {json:api} error object in a document's `errors` array.
- [@warp-drive/core/types/spec/json-api-raw](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/spec/json-api-raw.md): Types for raw {json:api} structures: resource objects, relationship objects, resource identifiers, links, meta and single, collection and empty documents.

###### /symbols

####### exports

- [RecordStore](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/symbols/variables/RecordStore.md): Internal symbol key under which a record instance keeps a reference to the store that owns it.
- [RequestSignature](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/symbols/variables/RequestSignature.md): Type-only symbol key that request builders set on the request they return so `store.request()` can infer the response type.
- [ResourceType](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/symbols/variables/ResourceType.md): Alias of the `Type` symbol that a record type can declare to tell WarpDrive APIs its resource type for better type inference.
- [TransformName](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/symbols/variables/TransformName.md): Alias of the `Type` symbol that a legacy transform can declare so `attr<Transform>('name')` checks the transform name at the type level.
- [Type](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/core/types/symbols/variables/Type.md): Symbol key that brands a record with its resource type for TypeScript, and names a derivation or transformation when it is registered.

#### @warp-drive/json-api

##### exports

- [JSONAPICache](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/json-api/classes/JSONAPICache.md): The JSON:API cache implementation: stores documents and normalized resources, tracks local, in-flight, and remote state, and manages relationships through the graph.

#### @warp-drive/utilities

- [@warp-drive/utilities/active-record](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/active-record.md): Request builders for find, query, create, update, and delete against ActiveRecord-style APIs with underscored plural URLs.
- [@warp-drive/utilities/derivations](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/derivations.md): The `concat` derivation, which joins a record's listed fields into one string with an optional separator.
- [@warp-drive/utilities/handlers](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/handlers.md): Ready-made request handlers for body compression, conditional handling, and meta-only responses, plus tracing helpers.
- [@warp-drive/utilities/json-api](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/json-api.md): Request builders and cache serializers for JSON:API servers, with dasherized plural URLs and configurable `Accept` headers.
- [@warp-drive/utilities/rest](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/rest.md): Request builders for find, query, create, update, and delete against REST APIs with camelCased plural URLs.
- [@warp-drive/utilities/string](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string.md): Cached case-conversion and English pluralization helpers, with configurable inflection rules, for mapping server names.

##### exports

- [buildBaseURL()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/functions/buildBaseURL.md): Joins host, namespace, resource path, id, and relationship field into a request URL without query params.
- [buildQueryParams()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/functions/buildQueryParams.md): Serializes query params into a string with keys and array values sorted, so equivalent queries share one URL.
- [filterEmpty()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/functions/filterEmpty.md): Returns a copy of an object without keys whose values are `undefined`, `null`, empty strings, or empty arrays.
- [setBuildURLConfig()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/functions/setBuildURLConfig.md): Sets the app-wide default `host` and `namespace` used by `buildBaseURL` and the request builders.
- [sortQueryParams()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/functions/sortQueryParams.md): Builds a `URLSearchParams` with keys and array values sorted, so equivalent queries produce identical params.

##### /active-record

###### exports

- [createRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/active-record/functions/createRecord.md): Builds a `POST` request that saves a newly created record, using ActiveRecord-style URLs.
- [deleteRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/active-record/functions/deleteRecord.md): Builds a `DELETE` request that persists deletion of an existing record, using ActiveRecord-style URLs.
- [findRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/active-record/functions/findRecord.md): Builds a `GET` request for one resource by type and id, using ActiveRecord-style pluralized, underscored URLs.
- [query()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/active-record/functions/query.md): Builds a `GET` request that queries a resource type with query params, using ActiveRecord-style URLs.
- [updateRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/active-record/functions/updateRecord.md): Builds a `PUT` (or `PATCH`) request that saves changes to an existing record, using ActiveRecord-style URLs.

##### /derivations

###### exports

- [concat](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/derivations/variables/concat.md): Derivation registered as `concat` that joins a record's listed `fields` into one string with an optional `separator`.

###### /Namespaces

- [@warp-drive/utilities/derivations/concat](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/derivations/namespaces/concat.md): Derivation registered as `concat` that joins a record's listed `fields` into one string with an optional `separator`.

##### /handlers

###### /Handlers

- [AutoCompress](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/handlers/classes/AutoCompress.md): Request handler that compresses large `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` bodies with `CompressionStream`, optionally streaming them.
- [Gate](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/handlers/classes/Gate.md): Request handler that wraps another handler and runs it only when a check function returns true for the request.
- [MetaDocHandler](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/handlers/variables/MetaDocHandler.md): Request handler that wraps the whole response body in `meta` for requests with `options.isMetaRequest` set.

###### /Constants

- [MAX_URL_LENGTH](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/handlers/variables/MAX_URL_LENGTH.md): The 8192-byte URL length limit, taken from AWS CloudFront, that `assertInvalidUrlLength` checks against.
- [SupportsRequestStreams](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/handlers/variables/SupportsRequestStreams.md): Whether the current browser can send a `ReadableStream` as a `fetch` request body, detected once at module load.
- [TAB_ASSIGNED](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/handlers/variables/TAB_ASSIGNED.md): Epoch seconds recorded when this module loaded, paired with `TAB_ID` in trace headers.
- [TAB_ID](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/handlers/variables/TAB_ID.md): Random UUID identifying the current browser tab, kept in `sessionStorage` across reloads, for request tracing.

###### /Utility Functions

- [addTraceHeader()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/handlers/functions/addTraceHeader.md): Sets an `X-Amzn-Trace-Id` header carrying a per-request id and the tab id, so requests can be traced to their browser tab.
- [assertInvalidUrlLength()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/handlers/functions/assertInvalidUrlLength.md): Dev-mode assertion that throws when a URL is longer than `MAX_URL_LENGTH`, suggesting a `POST` or `QUERY` request instead.

##### /json-api

###### exports

- [createRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/json-api/functions/createRecord.md): Builds a JSON:API `POST` request for saving a new record; the app must set the request body itself.
- [deleteRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/json-api/functions/deleteRecord.md): Builds a JSON:API `DELETE` request that persists deletion of an existing record.
- [findRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/json-api/functions/findRecord.md): Builds a JSON:API `GET` request for one resource by type and id, with optional `include`.
- [postQuery()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/json-api/functions/postQuery.md): Builds a JSON:API `POST` request that sends a query as the JSON body, cached under a key built from the query params.
- [query()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/json-api/functions/query.md): Builds a JSON:API `GET` request that queries a resource type, sending the query as URL query params.
- [serializePatch()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/json-api/functions/serializePatch.md): Serializes only a resource's changed attributes and relationships from the cache into a JSON:API-style `{ data }` patch.
- [serializeResources()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/json-api/functions/serializeResources.md): Copies the cached state of one or more resources into a JSON:API-style `{ data }` object, a starting point for request bodies.
- [setBuildURLConfig()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/json-api/functions/setBuildURLConfig.md): Sets the JSON:API extensions and profiles sent in the `Accept` header, plus the global URL host and namespace.
- [updateRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/json-api/functions/updateRecord.md): Builds a JSON:API `PUT` (or `PATCH`) request for saving an existing record; the app must set the request body itself.

##### /rest

###### exports

- [createRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/rest/functions/createRecord.md): Builds a `POST` request that saves a newly created record, using REST-style URLs.
- [deleteRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/rest/functions/deleteRecord.md): Builds a `DELETE` request that persists deletion of an existing record, using REST-style URLs.
- [findRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/rest/functions/findRecord.md): Builds a `GET` request for one resource by type and id, using REST-style pluralized, camelCased URLs.
- [query()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/rest/functions/query.md): Builds a `GET` request that queries a resource type with query params, using REST-style URLs.
- [updateRecord()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/rest/functions/updateRecord.md): Builds a `PUT` (or `PATCH`) request that saves changes to an existing record, using REST-style URLs.

##### /string

###### exports

- [dasherize](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/variables/dasherize.md): Converts camelCase, underscored, or spaced strings to dasherized form, such as `innerHTML` to `inner-html`.
- [camelize()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/camelize.md): Converts dashed, underscored, dotted, or spaced strings to lowerCamelCase, such as `action_name` to `actionName`.
- [capitalize()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/capitalize.md): Uppercases the first letter of a string, and of each `/`-separated path segment, leaving the rest unchanged.
- [clear()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/clear.md): Empties the cached results of `singularize` and `pluralize` while keeping all inflection rules.
- [clearRules()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/clearRules.md): Removes every inflection rule, including the defaults, and empties the `singularize` and `pluralize` caches.
- [irregular()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/irregular.md): Registers a singular and plural word pair that `pluralize` and `singularize` map directly instead of applying rules.
- [loadIrregular()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/loadIrregular.md): Registers a list of singular and plural word pairs that `pluralize` and `singularize` map directly.
- [loadUncountable()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/loadUncountable.md): Registers a list of words that `pluralize` and `singularize` should always return unchanged.
- [plural()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/plural.md): Adds a regex and replacement rule that `pluralize` checks before all existing plural rules.
- [pluralize()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/pluralize.md): Returns the plural form of an English word using the registered inflection rules, with cached results.
- [resetToDefaults()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/resetToDefaults.md): Discards all custom inflection rules and caches, then restores the built-in default rules.
- [setMaxLRUCacheSize()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/setMaxLRUCacheSize.md): Sets how many results the `camelize`, `underscore`, `capitalize`, and `dasherize` caches each keep (default 10,000).
- [singular()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/singular.md): Adds a regex and replacement rule that `singularize` checks before all existing singular rules.
- [singularize()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/singularize.md): Returns the singular form of an English word using the registered inflection rules, with cached results.
- [uncountable()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/uncountable.md): Registers a word that `pluralize` and `singularize` should always return unchanged.
- [underscore()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/utilities/string/functions/underscore.md): Converts camelCase, dashed, or spaced strings to lowercase snake_case, such as `innerHTML` to `inner_html`.

#### @warp-drive/experiments

- [@warp-drive/experiments/data-worker](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/data-worker.md): Experimental `DataWorker`, which runs a store inside a Worker or SharedWorker, and the `CacheHandler` it uses to serve requests from its in-memory or persisted cache.
- [@warp-drive/experiments/document-storage](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/document-storage.md): Experimental `DocumentStorage`, a persistent store for request documents and their resources backed by the Origin Private File System and synced across tabs.
- [@warp-drive/experiments/image-fetch](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/image-fetch.md): Experimental main-thread client for loading images through an `ImageWorker` running in a SharedWorker.
- [@warp-drive/experiments/image-worker](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/image-worker.md): Experimental worker-side image loader that fetches and caches images for main-thread `ImageFetch` clients.
- [@warp-drive/experiments/pagination](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/pagination.md): Experimental reactive pagination primitives for tracking page state, links, and caches across paginated requests.
- [@warp-drive/experiments/storage](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage.md): Experimental reactive wrappers over localStorage, sessionStorage and the Cache API, with decorators such as `LocalResource` and `param` that bind class fields to storage or query params.
- [@warp-drive/experiments/worker-fetch](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/worker-fetch.md): Experimental `WorkerFetch` request handler that sends requests from the main thread to a `DataWorker` and settles them with its responses.

##### /data-worker

###### exports

- [DataWorker](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/data-worker/classes/DataWorker.md)
- [CacheHandler](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/data-worker/variables/CacheHandler.md): Experimental cache handler for a DataWorker that serves requests from the in-memory or persisted cache and returns documents hydrated with their resources.

##### /document-storage

###### exports

- [DocumentStorage](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/document-storage/classes/DocumentStorage.md): Experimental persistent store for request documents and their resources, backed by the Origin Private File System and synced across tabs via `BroadcastChannel`.

##### /image-fetch

###### exports

- [ImageFetch](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/image-fetch/classes/ImageFetch.md): Experimental main-thread client that asks an `ImageWorker` to load image urls and resolves with cached object urls.

##### /image-worker

###### exports

- [ImageWorker](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/image-worker/classes/ImageWorker.md): Experimental worker-side image loader that fetches images for connected `ImageFetch` clients and returns deduped, cached object urls.

##### /pagination

###### exports

- [defaultPageHints](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/pagination/variables/defaultPageHints.md): Experimental: the fallback page-hints function, reading `meta.page` or `meta.currentPage` and `meta.totalPages` from a document, with `0` meaning unknown.
- [clearPaginationCache()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/pagination/functions/clearPaginationCache.md): Experimental: discards every shared pagination cache, mainly so tests start from a clean state.
- [createPaginationLinksSubscription()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/pagination/functions/createPaginationLinksSubscription.md): Experimental: creates the subscription a pagination links component such as `<EachLink />` uses to derive navigation links from a paged pagination state.
- [createPaginationSubscription()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/pagination/functions/createPaginationSubscription.md): Experimental: creates the subscription that manages a `<Paginate />` component's initial request lifecycle and pagination state, for managing that lifecycle yourself.
- [getPaginationCache()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/pagination/functions/getPaginationCache.md): Experimental: returns the shared pagination cache for a collection's `first` or `self` link, creating it on first use.
- [getPaginationLinks()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/pagination/functions/getPaginationLinks.md): Experimental: returns the navigation links for a paged pagination state, creating them on first call and returning the same instance for the same state.
- [getPaginationState()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/pagination/functions/getPaginationState.md): Experimental: returns the pagination state for a request, creating it on first call and returning the same instance for the same request thereafter.

##### /storage

###### exports

- [CacheStorage](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/classes/CacheStorage.md): Experimental `Storage`-compatible interface over the browser Cache API, suited to larger JSON data sets than localStorage.
- [DEFAULT_CACHE_ID](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/variables/DEFAULT_CACHE_ID.md)
- [_initializeFields()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/functions/initializeFields.md)
- [BooleanParam()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/functions/BooleanParam.md): Experimental helper that creates a query-param config serializing a boolean field as '1' when true and omitting it when false.
- [CacheResource()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/functions/CacheResource.md): Experimental class decorator that turns a class into a reactive resource whose fields persist via the Cache API and are shared across tabs.
- [configureLocalStorage()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/functions/configureLocalStorage.md): Experimental function that sets fallback and quota-handling options for the reactive localStorage singleton before its first use.
- [configureSessionStorage()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/functions/configureSessionStorage.md): Experimental function that sets fallback and quota-handling options for the reactive sessionStorage singleton before its first use.
- [effect()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/functions/effect.md): Experimental field decorator for storage resources that runs a callback when the stored value changes in another tab or window.
- [field()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/functions/field.md): Experimental decorator that makes a storage resource property a reactive field persisted to local, session, or cache storage.
- [getCacheStorage()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/functions/getCacheStorage.md)
- [getLocalStorage()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/functions/getLocalStorage.md): Experimental function that returns the shared reactive wrapper around localStorage, creating it on first call.
- [getSessionStorage()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/functions/getSessionStorage.md)
- [input()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/functions/input.md)
- [LocalResource()](https://canary.warp-drive.io/api/@warp-drive/experiments/storage/functions/LocalResource.md): Experimental class decorator that turns a class into a reactive resource whose fields persist in localStorage.
